root_cause.text: In retry_aligned_read(), releasing an overlapped stripe via raid5_release_stripe() places it on the released_stripes llist, which gets drained onto handle_list by release_stripe_list() in the same raid5d loop, but before handle_stripe() can process it, retry_aligned_read() re-fetches and removes the stripe from handle_list via find_get_stripe()—creating an infinite loop that prevents the overlap from being resolved.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "When retry_aligned_read() encounters an overlapped stripe, it releases the stripe via raid5_release_stripe() which puts it on the lockless released_stripes llist. In the next raid5d loop iteration, release_stripe_list() drains the stripe onto handle_list (since STRIPE_HANDLE is set by the original IO), but retry_aligned_read() runs before handle_active_stripes() and removes the stripe from handle_list via find_get_stripe() -> list_del_init(). This prevents handle_stripe() from ever processing the stripe to resolve the overlap, causing an infinite loop and soft lockup." The patch replaces raid5_release_stripe() with __release_stripe() using temp_inactive_list to avoid this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix race condition and incorrect stripe release by acquiring device_lock and using per-hash inactive list when releasing stripe after add_stripe_bio fails in retry_aligned_read.
intent_record.what: Replaced a call to raid5_release_stripe(sh) with code that acquires device_lock, retrieves the stripe's hash_lock_index, calls __release_stripe(conf, sh, &conf->temp_inactive_list[hash]) while holding the lock, and releases the lock.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when add_stripe_bio fails in retry_aligned_read, the stripe head is released under proper locking (device_lock) and placed on the correct per-hash temp_inactive_list, preventing race conditions and ensuring correct list management.

grouping_result.intent: Fix race condition and incorrect stripe release by acquiring device_lock and using per-hash inactive list when releasing stripe after add_stripe_bio fails in retry_aligned_read.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly address the stripe release mechanism in retry_aligned_read(), which is the same function involved in the vulnerability's infinite loop. Acquiring device_lock and using per-hash inactive list modifies how the stripe is released after add_stripe_bio fails, potentially preventing the re-fetching that causes the loop.

candidates.rationale: Releasing the stripe via raid5_release_stripe() places it on the released_stripes llist, which gets drained onto handle_list. This allows retry_aligned_read() to re-fetch the stripe before handle_stripe() processes the overlap, leading to an infinite loop.

Setting conf->retry_read_aligned causes retry_aligned_read() to be re-invoked in the same raid5d loop, enabling the re-fetch of the just-released stripe from handle_list before handle_stripe() can resolve the overlap.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement releases the stripe via raid5_release_stripe(), placing it on the released_stripes llist. In the same raid5d loop, release_stripe_list() drains this llist onto handle_list, allowing retry_aligned_read() to re-fetch the stripe via find_get_stripe() before handle_stripe() can process the overlap, creating an infinite loop.

This statement sets conf->retry_read_aligned to the current raid_bio, causing retry_aligned_read() to be re-invoked in the same raid5d loop. This re-invocation enables the re-fetch of the just-released stripe from handle_list, preventing the overlap from being resolved and perpetuating the infinite loop.
